Priya —

Thanks for the note and the clear ask. Short answer up front: platform fee is a one‑time implementation amortized for billing guidance but contractually a monthly-recognized platform entitlement; the ops surcharge is configurable — either one‑time professional services pass‑through or a small recurring ops retainer depending on the support SLA you choose.

I attached a quick amortization worksheet and a one‑page appendix that maps support tiers to the recurring ops uplift. High level:
- 12‑month pilot example: platform fee $120k amortized over 12 months = $10k/month on the invoice (but invoice shows platform fee as a separate line item to support capitalization requests)
- 36‑month term: same $120k amortized = $3.33k/month (lower monthly impact)
- Ops surcharge options:
  • Ad‑hoc PS pass‑through: billed as time & materials on completion of milestones (no recurring uplift)
  • Ops retainer (recommended for production readiness): $4k/month for 24/7 monitoring + automated oncall routing; includes two 1‑day migration windows and a quarterly health check

If you want, we can step through a blended invoice mock for both scenarios. Looping in Marissa (Commercial) to confirm discount levers for pilot -> enterprise conversion.

Regards,
David Kim
Senior Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: PlatformFee_Amortization_worksheet.xlsx]

Subject: Internal: Helix pricing levers for pilot conversion

David —

Notes from our side and what we can offer:
1) Platform fee: standard is $120k for the private deploy starter pack (on‑prem connectors, 1x support engineer for cutover). For pilots under $150k ARR, we can offer 50% of the platform fee as a credit on first renewal if they convert to a 36-month committed contract within 9 months of deployment.
2) Ops surcharge: we treat this as two components — a one‑time migration T&M estimate (typically $12k–$24k depending on data size) plus a monthly ops retainer if they want 24/7. For enterprise SLA we recommend the ops retainer.
3) Discounting: because Helix is a mid‑market account but with regulated health data, we can provide a 10% commercial discount on consumption for the first 12 months if they commit to a 24‑month term and accept the ops retainer.

Karthik — any constraints on stretching the pilot amortization offer (50% credit) to 60% if we get a legal signature within 180 days?

—Marissa
Director, Commercial Strategy, Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com
Date: 2026-07-22T14:44:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: Helix pricing levers for pilot conversion

Marissa —

We can flex to 60% platform fee credit but only if we secure a 36‑month committed spend floor (minimum ARR threshold) and include a 6‑month non‑cancellable ops retainer at the enterprise SLA level. That protects us from churn and amortizes our implementation cost. Also recommend capping any one‑time migration T&M at $30k in the SOW to keep procurement comfortable.

I'll have Legal draft a short addendum for the pilot credit and non‑cancellable ops term. Once we have Priya's greenlight on the terms in email, David — please send her the invoice mock showing both scenarios.

Karthik
VP, Enterprise Pricing

Priya —

Appreciate the patience. Attached is a concise proposal that shows two invoice mocks side by side: 12‑month pilot (no committed ARR) and 36‑month committed conversion with the pilot credit applied. Summary callouts:
• Pilot (12 months): platform fee $120k listed as "Platform entitlement (amortized)" $10k/mo; optional migration T&M estimated at $18k; no recurring ops uplift unless you elect the retainer.
• Commit (36 months): effective monthly platform entitlement $3.33k/mo; pilot credit 60% applied to the platform fee (per Karthik's approval) if Helix signs the 36‑month SOW within 180 days; 6‑month non‑cancellable ops retainer at enterprise SLA required for the credit. In plain terms, net platform fee on first invoice becomes $48k and remaining $72k is amortized per the contract schedule.

If the economic model looks good I can schedule a short call with Finance and Legal tomorrow to walk through the invoice and the addendum language.

Thanks —
David
